scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a missing OSPF network statement on switch_dist_1_1 for its
LAN-side subnet 10.1.1.0/24. The router's FRR configuration under "router
ospf" contains only "network 172.16.0.6/31 area 1", which covers the uplink
to router_core_1 but omits the br0 interface (10.1.1.1/24) that serves
host_1_1_1_1. As a result, 10.1.1.0/24 is never injected into OSPF and no
stub-network LSA for it appears in Area 1 or Area 0. Every other router in
the fabric — router_core_1, router_core_2, router_core_3,
switch_server_access, switch_dist_2_1 — is therefore unaware that 10.1.1.0/24
exists.

This produces the exact symptom pattern described in the ticket: host_1_1_1_1
can ping its gateway (10.1.1.1 lives on br0 of switch_dist_1_1 and is
directly reachable), and switch_dist_1_1 itself can reach the server farm
(it has OSPF-learned routes via its eth0 uplink). However, when host_1_1_1_1
sends a packet to, say, 10.200.0.3, switch_dist_1_1 forwards it upstream
correctly, but the reply destined for 10.1.1.2 arrives at router_core_1/
router_core_3/switch_server_access with no matching route entry — the packet
is silently dropped, producing the 100% silent loss seen in testing. Pod 2 is
unaffected because switch_dist_2_1's config correctly includes both "network
10.2.1.0/24 area 1" and "network 172.16.0.8/31 area 1".

Root cause: switch_dist_1_1's OSPF network statement is missing the
"network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1" line.

Corrective fix: on switch_dist_1_1, enter vtysh and add under "router ospf":
  network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1
This will cause br0's subnet to be flooded as a stub network in Area 1,
router_core_1 (the ABR) will summarise it into Area 0, and all routers will
install the return-path route within one OSPF Hello interval.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1 as the affected device and describes its missing OSPF network statement.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies that switch_dist_1_1 is missing the 'network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1' OSPF statement, so the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix is not advertised.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: Agent clearly explains that switch_dist_1_1 advertises uplink but not the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet, causing the network to lack a return route while the forward path still works (reply packets are dropped).

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis notes that switch_dist_1_1 has OSPF-learned routes via its uplink (the 172.16.0.6/31 network), which explains why the switch’s own traffic reaches the farm despite the missing LAN network statement.
Recommends adding the missing 'network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1' under router ospf on switch_dist_1_1, which matches the expected corrective action.

The log contains direct evidence: switch_dist_1_1's running-config omits the 10.1.1.0/24 network statement, router_core_1's routing/OSPF DB lack the prefix, and pings show asymmetric loss — so the agent's conclusion that the missing OSPF advertisement causes the return-path failure is well supported.
